seo.title: Best Ful Medames in Cairo (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the 12 best Ful Medames spots in Cairo for 2026. From legendary street stalls to modern cafes, find your perfect bowl of Egypt's beloved breakfast dish. Authentic flavors, local favorites & insider tips.

hero.subtitle: Ful Medames, the quintessential Egyptian breakfast, is a hearty, flavorful dish of slow-cooked fava beans, served in countless variations across Cairo. It's more than just food; it's a cultural cornerstone.

picks.name: El Gahsh
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A legendary institution, El Gahsh has been serving its iconic ful for decades from a humble, bustling storefront. Known for its perfectly creamy, slow-cooked beans, it's a must-visit for anyone seeking the true taste of Cairo's breakfast staple. The atmosphere is vibrant, authentically Egyptian, and unpretentious.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful medames bil zeit (with oil and a squeeze of lemon), served with fresh baladi bread and pickled vegetables.
picks.insiderTip: Go early in the morning to experience the true breakfast rush. Be prepared to stand or share a small table, and don't be shy about ordering extra bread.
picks.redditQuote: "Honestly, you haven't truly had ful until you've been to El Gahsh. The texture of their ful is just unmatched, so creamy!"

picks.name: Felfela
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Felfela is more than just a restaurant; it's a cultural landmark. While it caters to tourists, locals still flock here for its wide array of classic Egyptian dishes, including excellent ful. The decor is charmingly eclectic with an old-world charm, featuring taxidermy animals and intricate details.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful Felfela (their signature blend, often with butter and spices) or Ful Iskandarani (spicy, with peppers and tomatoes).
picks.insiderTip: Visit the take-out window for a quicker, more budget-friendly ful sandwich experience, then find a bench nearby to people-watch.
picks.redditQuote: "Felfela is a solid choice, especially if you're downtown. Their ful is consistently good, even if it's a bit more 'tourist-friendly' now."

picks.name: Gad
picks.whyItMadeTheList: With numerous branches across Cairo, Gad is a household name for quick, satisfying Egyptian meals. Their ful is consistently good, offering a reliable option for both breakfast and quick bites throughout the day. It's clean, efficient, and a popular choice for families and locals alike.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with pastrami or a mix of ful and ta'ameya (falafel) in a sandwich for a hearty meal.
picks.insiderTip: Gad is perfect for a quick, no-fuss meal. Their cleanliness and quick service make it a safe bet, especially for first-timers in Cairo.
picks.redditQuote: "You can always count on Gad for a decent, quick ful. It's not the most 'authentic' but it's consistent and reliable, especially in a hurry."

picks.name: Zooba
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Zooba offers a contemporary take on Egyptian street food classics, serving up ful with a gourmet twist in a stylish, vibrant setting. Their commitment to fresh, high-quality ingredients shines through in every dish. It's a great spot for those looking for a slightly more upscale and aesthetically pleasing experience.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with butter & eggs, or the spicy ful with chili oil. Don't miss their fresh juices and ta'ameya (falafel).
picks.insiderTip: Zooba is fantastic for a brunch with friends. Try their different bread options and sauces to customize your ful experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Zooba's ful is amazing if you want something a bit different and cleaner. Definitely a step up from typical street food, and their branding is on point."

picks.name: El Tabei
picks.whyItMadeTheList: El Tabei is a beloved local spot renowned for its exceptional ful. It might not have the historical gravitas of El Gahsh, but its dedication to simple, delicious preparation has earned it a loyal following. The atmosphere is casual and community-focused, reflecting the heart of Maadi.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful Medames with tahini and a side of their perfectly cooked eggs. Ask for 'ful by the pottery' for a traditional serving.
picks.insiderTip: This spot is popular among Maadi residents for good reason. Arrive before noon on weekends to beat the biggest rush and enjoy a relaxed breakfast.
picks.redditQuote: "Every time I'm in Maadi, El Tabei is my go-to for ful. Their beans are always perfectly seasoned and the tahini is fresh."

picks.name: Abou Rabea
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tucked away in the vibrant Shoubra district, Abou Rabea is a true neighborhood gem, cherished by locals for its authentic and flavorful ful. It's a no-frills establishment that focuses purely on the quality of its food. The bustling environment offers a glimpse into local Cairo life.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with linseed oil (zeit har) for a nutty flavor, or the spicy ful with green chili peppers.
picks.insiderTip: Shoubra can be busy, so consider taking a taxi or ride-sharing service. Combine your ful experience with a stroll through the lively streets of Shoubra.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want real Shoubra ful, Abou Rabea is where it's at. No fancy stuff, just damn good ful that tastes like grandma made it."

picks.name: Kazaz
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Kazaz has been serving generations of Cairenes with its wide selection of Egyptian dishes. While known for many things, their ful Medames maintains a high standard, prepared with care and served in a more traditional restaurant setting. It's a reliable choice for a comfortable, sit-down meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Their classic Ful Medames, perhaps with a side of Shakshuka (eggs cooked in tomato sauce) for a full breakfast spread.
picks.insiderTip: Kazaz is great if you prefer a more formal setting than a street stall but still want authentic flavors. They also have excellent pastries.
picks.redditQuote: "Kazaz is an old-school favorite. Their ful is consistently solid, and you can get a whole breakfast experience there, not just ful."

picks.name: Al-Ezaby
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Al-Ezaby is a well-regarded local spot in Heliopolis, famous for its simple yet delicious Egyptian breakfast fare. The focus here is on quality and consistency, offering perfectly cooked ful in a clean, no-frills environment. It's a go-to for many residents starting their day.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with butter and a sprinkle of cumin, served piping hot with freshly baked bread.
picks.insiderTip: Perfect for a quick, affordable, and authentic breakfast if you're in the Heliopolis area. Expect a steady stream of locals picking up their morning meals.
picks.redditQuote: "For a reliable ful in Heliopolis, Al-Ezaby is always a good bet. Their beans are always soft and flavorful, never dry."

picks.name: Om Hassan
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Om Hassan offers a taste of home-cooked Egyptian food, and their ful Medames is no exception. Prepared with traditional recipes and a generous hand, it evokes the warmth and comfort of a meal made by an Egyptian mother. It's a charming spot favored by locals for its genuine flavors.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with green salad and ta'ameya for a classic, filling Egyptian breakfast combo.
picks.insiderTip: This is a great place to experience the hospitality of a smaller, family-run eatery. Don't be afraid to ask for recommendations on other traditional dishes.
picks.redditQuote: "Om Hassan's ful reminds me of my grandmother's cooking. It's just simple, honest, and incredibly comforting."

picks.name: Al-Sayeda Nafisa
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Named after the revered mosque nearby, Al-Sayeda Nafisa is a quintessential street-side ful vendor in the historic Sayeda Zeinab district. This humble spot focuses on simplicity and speed, serving up delicious, no-frills ful that's a staple for workers and early risers. It's the epitome of Cairo's street food scene.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with plain oil and a side of fresh onions for a truly authentic street food experience.
picks.insiderTip: This is a standing or grab-and-go spot. Be quick with your order and enjoy your ful while observing the vibrant street life around you.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're in Sayeda Zeinab, you HAVE to grab ful from Al-Sayeda Nafisa. It's cheap, fast, and exactly what street ful should taste like."

picks.name: Abou Hassan
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Abou Hassan in Dokki is another long-standing local favorite, known for its consistent quality and straightforward approach to ful. It's a humble shop with a loyal clientele who appreciate its authentic flavors and friendly service. A great option for a delicious and affordable breakfast.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful with butter, or the refreshing Ful with yogurt and a drizzle of olive oil, if available.
picks.insiderTip: This place gets busy during morning rush hours. It's a small space, so be prepared for a lively atmosphere, but the wait is usually short.
picks.redditQuote: "Abou Hassan in Dokki is my morning ritual. Their ful is just perfect, simple but so flavorful. Never disappoints."

picks.name: El-Zahra
picks.whyItMadeTheList: El-Zahra is a well-established breakfast spot in Dokki, popular among residents for its reliable and delicious Egyptian fare, particularly its ful. They offer various ful preparations, ensuring there's something for everyone. It's a clean, casual environment perfect for a morning meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Ful Medames with tahini and a side of their fresh bread, or a hearty ful and eggs plate.
picks.insiderTip: They often have a variety of pickles and salads available to accompany your ful, so make sure to ask for the full spread.
picks.redditQuote: "Whenever I'm in Dokki and need a quick, satisfying ful, El-Zahra is always a good choice. Their ful is consistently good, no complaints."

faq.question: What is Ful Medames?
faq.answer: Ful Medames is a traditional Egyptian dish consisting of slow-cooked fava beans, seasoned with various spices and oils, and often served with fresh bread. It's a staple breakfast and often lunch meal, beloved for its hearty, nutritious, and affordable qualities across all social classes.

faq.question: When is the best time to eat Ful Medames in Cairo?
faq.answer: While traditionally a breakfast dish, Ful Medames is enjoyed throughout the day in Cairo, often for a late breakfast or a casual lunch. Many vendors open very early in the morning and close in the late afternoon. For the freshest taste and a vibrant atmosphere, mornings are ideal.

faq.question: What are the common variations of Ful Medames?
faq.answer: Ful Medames comes in many forms: 'ful bil zeit' (with oil), 'ful bil tahini' (with sesame paste), 'ful iskandarani' (spicy with peppers and tomatoes), 'ful bil beid' (with eggs), and 'ful sada' (plain). Many places also offer variations with butter, pastrami, or various herbs.

faq.question: Is Ful Medames vegetarian/vegan-friendly?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Ful Medames is inherently a plant-based dish, made from fava beans. Most basic preparations with oil, tahini, or tomatoes are vegan. If you're vegan, simply specify 'ful sada' or 'bil zeit' and ensure no butter or animal fats are added, though these are typically optional toppings anyway.

faq.question: How much does a typical Ful Medames meal cost in Cairo?
faq.answer: A basic ful sandwich can cost as little as EGP 10-20 ($0.30-0.65) from a street cart. A generous plate of ful with bread and accompaniments at a casual eatery typically ranges from EGP 20-70 ($0.65-2.30) per person, making it one of Cairo's most budget-friendly and filling meals.

faq.question: What should I eat with Ful Medames?
faq.answer: Ful is almost always served with fresh Egyptian 'aish baladi' (pita-like bread) for scooping. Common accompaniments include pickled vegetables (torshi), fresh tomatoes and cucumbers, green salad, fried or boiled eggs, and sometimes ta'ameya (Egyptian falafel) for a complete breakfast feast.

We prioritized authenticity, flavor variety, hygiene, and overall dining experience, ensuring a comprehensive guide for every palate.
